prompt: Pull the host, port and path out of a URL string using java.net.URI, filling in the default port when the URL leaves it out. Complete the three methods in UrlParts, then run the tests.
explanation: java.net.URI parses a URL into labelled pieces, so you never have to hunt for slashes and colons yourself. getPort() returns -1 when the URL carries no explicit port, which is the signal to fall back to the scheme default -- 443 for https, 80 otherwise. getPath() returns an empty string for a bare host like http://example.com, so an empty result becomes "/", and the query string is kept out of the path automatically.
hints: URI.create(url) gives you a URI object with getHost(), getPort(), getScheme() and getPath() already separated.
getPort() answers -1 when the URL has no ':port' part -- treat that as 'use the default' rather than as a real port number.
getPath() can come back empty (or null) for a URL like http://example.com, so test for that before returning it.
